newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian judge sacked from child sex probe.
newsitem.headline: Belgian judge sacked from child sex probe.

text.p: Belgium's highest court decided on Monday that a magistrate investigating a case of child sex, kidnapping and murder had compromised himself and could not be allowed to continue the investigation.
The Cour de Cassation said it upheld formal complaints from lawyers representing the two main defendants in the so-called Dutroux case in which four young girls have been found dead.
"The decision was made...given that the impartiality of magistrates was a fundamental rule," President Oscar Stranard told a packed court.

Outside the Justice Palace in central Brussels Connerotte supporters booed the news under the watchful eye of dozens policemen. A crowd of some 700 protestors chanted "Assassins, assassins" after the announcement.
A very emotional Paul Marchal, father of Ann Marchal who died at the hands of the Dutroux gang, said, "it is the beginning of the end... justice is dead."

The lawyers for convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux and Brussels businessman Michel Nihoul had said investigating magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte had shown bias for the victims by attending a pasta party for two girls rescued from Dutroux.
However, the case will stay in Neufchateau in the hands of Connerotte's boss, regional public prosecutor Michel Bourlet.

"The fact that it remains in Neufchateau is a very important element because it means Bourlet will remain in charge," Laurent Arnauts, the lawyer for the parents of missing child Loubna Benaissa, told Reuters after the ruling.

Under Belgian law an investigating magistrate must be strictly neutral in his quest for the truth. He must put together two case files, one with facts indicting a suspect and one with facts supporting any claims of innocence.
On the basis of the files the public prosecutor must decide whether any charges will stand up in court.

The complaints from the lawyers caused consternation among ordinary Belgians who have a high regard for Connerotte's successes in the Dutroux case and who saw his presence at the pasta party as an act of humanity.
